messages:
Tom Nguyen (Customer): we've started seeing bursts of 429s from our private gateway since we switched the k8s ingress to the new autoscaler policy. latency also spikes to 1.8s for small requests. happening every ~2m for a few seconds.
Alice Rivera (Support): thanks Tom — can you paste the ingress annotations + the gateway/rate-limiter config? Also a short curl showing the 429 response headers would help (we're looking for Retry-After, x-ratelimit-*).
Tom Nguyen (Customer): here's the ingress annotations and envoy config we applied last night:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: ai-gateway
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: "nginx"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "20"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: "600"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "5"
spec:
  rules:
  - host: api.customer.example
    http:
      paths: ...
```
and the envoy rate limit filter is pointing at our redis cluster with domain "redwood-cust".
Curl output (truncated):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-length: 0
x-envoy-ratelimited: 1
```
No Retry-After header.
Alice Rivera (Support): OK, two quick thoughts: lack of Retry-After can make clients retry aggressively. Also nginx limit-rpm + limit-burst are in the ingress controller — they interact badly with the gateway-level token-bucket in Envoy. If both are enforcing, bursts get clipped unpredictably.
Ben Cho (SRE): can you share a short time-window of logs from the gateway (kubectl logs) around a spike? Specifically need the envoy ratelimit responses and any 5xxs from the upstream. Also tell us if your ingress controller is the nginx controller or the cloud one.
Tom Nguyen (Customer): nginx controller (community/nginx-ingress v1.15). logs: 
```
[2026-03-12T02:21:11Z] "POST /v1/generate" 200 512ms
[2026-03-12T02:23:09Z] "POST /v1/generate" 429 15ms x-envoy-ratelimited
[2026-03-12T02:23:10Z] "POST /v1/generate" 429 8ms x-envoy-ratelimited
[2026-03-12T02:23:10Z] "POST /v1/generate" 200 1.2s
```
we're seeing a flurry of 429s for 10-12s every ~2min.
Rajesh Iyer (Eng - Runtime): this pattern looks like two-tier rate limiting contention. The ingress rate limiter is configured for per-IP buckets (limit-rpm + burst), while Envoy (gateway) is using a service-wide token bucket keyed by API key. When the ingress clips connections it produces a condensed set of requests hitting Envoy all at once, which then exhausts the service bucket and returns 429 with no Retry-After if not configured.
Alice Rivera (Support): for a quick mitigation: either relax the ingress limits (increase limit-burst to 50 and limit-rpm to 1200) or disable ingress-level limiting and let Envoy do the throttling (the gateway has better visibility into API keys). We'd prefer disabling duplicate enforcement.
Maya Patel (CS): if they relax ingress, we should watch billing/units — bursts may spike token usage. Tom, do you have telemetry retention for token counts?
Tom Nguyen (Customer): we do. short term we can relax ingress. what's the recommended ingress annotation values for stable bursts?
Ben Cho (SRE): recommended starting point for nginx controller: limit-rpm: "1200", limit-burst: "50" and limit-connections: "100". But more importantly, switch the ingress limiter key to $binary_remote_addr + request_uri if you're proxying multi-tenant requests from same IPs. Example annotation:
```yaml
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-key: "$binary_remote_addr$request_uri"
```
That avoids all clients from one IP sharing the same token pool.
Rajesh Iyer (Eng - Runtime): also add Retry-After headers from the gateway side. In Envoy ratelimit config set the HTTP response headers on over-limit to include Retry-After with a sensible backoff. And consider a per-api-key local token cache (leaky bucket local) so short bursts don't always hit the central redis rate limiter.
Alice Rivera (Support): to reproduce locally we used this scenario: 10 clients each fire 10 requests in 2s to the same API key, ingress limit-burst at 5 -> results in ingress cut then sudden flood to gateway once connections re-open -> gateway bucket exhausted -> 429 avalanche. If you can reproduce, please share the small k6 script and we'll iterate.
Tom Nguyen (Customer): here's a tiny repro k6 script (we ran it from within cluster):
```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function() {
  for (let i=0;i<10;i++) { http.post('https://api.customer.example/v1/generate', '{"prompt":"hi"}'); }
  sleep(1);
}
```
Ben Cho (SRE): good. For immediate patch: 1) bump ingress limit-burst to 50, 2) set limit-key to include request_uri, 3) enable Retry-After in Envoy (Rajesh can share the exact filter snippet). We'll monitor for 30m.
Rajesh Iyer (Eng - Runtime): envoy filter snippet to add Retry-After on over-limit (example):
```yaml
rate_limit_service:
  timeout: 2s
  failure_mode_deny: false
  on_over_limit: { response_headers_to_add: [{ append_action: "REPLACE", header: { key: "Retry-After", value: "5" } }] }
```
Alice Rivera (Support): Tom, once you apply the ingress changes can you post new logs for 10m after? We'll watch for 429 rate and also CPU on the redis rate-limit store.
Tom Nguyen (Customer): applying now, will report back in 15m. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ratebot: deployment: ingress patch rolled to ai-gateway namespace by tom - rollout in progress :spinner:
Tom Nguyen (Customer): update — after bumping burst to 50 and changing limit-key we still see tiny 429 spikes but way shorter (2-3s) and no longer cascades. CPU on redis dropped ~30%. Looks much better.
Alice Rivera (Support): great — we'll advise permanent changes: leave ingress limits as guardrails but set higher bursts, switch to api-key policing at gateway, enable Retry-After, and add local token caching in Envoy if you need microsecond-level smoothing. I'll open a follow-up ticket with recommended YAMLs and a runbook for testing.
Maya Patel (CS): looping in account team to adjust billing alerting thresholds.
Tom Nguyen (Customer): appreciated, saved our production windows.
Alice Rivera (Support): closing this thread when runbook created. if anything flares up ping us in #support and we'll reopen. :white_check_mark:
